[{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"Prove that, the angle inscribed in the semi-circle is a right angle.","marks":2,"answer":"Suppose PQ is the diameter of a circle with center O. \(\angle PRQ\) is the semicircular angle.
- The circular angle standing on the arc PAQ, \(\angle PRQ = \frac{1}{2}\) (central straight angle \(\angle POQ\)).
- But straight angle \(\angle POQ = 2\) right angles.
- Therefore, \(\angle PRQ = \frac{1}{2} \times 2\) right angles = 1 right angle. (Proved)
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207827902_oycx0s.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207827902_oycx0s.jpeg"},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Prove that, P is the middle point of AB.","marks":4,"answer":"Suppose AB is a chord of circle ABC with center O. OP ⊥ AB.
- In \(\triangle AOB\), OA = OB (radii).
- In \(\triangle OAP\) and \(\triangle OBP\):
\(\angle OPA = \angle OPB = 1\) right angle (since OP ⊥ AB),
OA = OB,
OP is common.
- Therefore, \(\triangle OAP \cong \triangle OBP\) (hypotenuse-side).
- Hence, AP = BP, so P is the midpoint of AB. (Proved)
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207827903_g5e4sc.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207827903_g5e4sc.jpeg"},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Prove that, OP = OQ.","marks":4,"answer":"Given AB = CD, OP ⊥ AB, OQ ⊥ CD.
- Perpendicular from center bisects chord: AP = BP, CQ = DQ.
- Since AB = CD, \(2AP = 2CQ \Rightarrow AP = CQ\).
- In right-angled \(\triangle OAP\) and \(\triangle OCQ\):
Hypotenuse OA = Hypotenuse OC (radii),
AP = CQ.
- Therefore, \(\triangle OAP \cong \triangle OCQ\) (hypotenuse-side).
- Hence, OP = OQ. (Proved)
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207827903_2i9wy4.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207827903_2i9wy4.jpeg"}]

parts:
[{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"What is the magnitude of the ∠QOS?","marks":2,"answer":"In the figure, OP = OQ, ∠OPQ = 30°.
- Angle at center ∠QOS = 2 × angle at circumference ∠SPQ (same arc QS).
- ∠SPQ = 30°, so ∠QOS = 2 × 30° = 60°. (Ans.)
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207829962_kcism8.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207829962_kcism8.jpeg"},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Prove that, PR = QR.","marks":4,"answer":"Given OR ⊥ PQ.
- In △ORP and △ORQ:
∠ORP = ∠ORQ = 1 right angle,
Hypotenuse OP = Hypotenuse OQ (radii),
OR is common.
- Therefore, △ORP ≅ △ORQ (hypotenuse-side).
- Hence, PR = QR. (Proved)
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207829963_imnludc.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207829963_imnludc.jpeg"},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Show that, the ratio of area of ΔQOS and circular segment QOS is 3√3 : 2π.","marks":4,"answer":"Let radius = r.
- Area of sector QOS = (60/360) × πr² = πr²/6.
- Area of △QOS = (1/2) × OS × OQ × sin 60° = (1/2) × r × r × (√3/2) = (√3r²)/4.
- Area of circular segment QOS = Area of sector - Area of triangle = πr²/6 - √3r²/4.
- Ratio of △QOS to segment QOS = (√3r²/4) / (πr²/6 - √3r²/4)
= (√3r²/4) / [(2πr² - 3√3r²)/12]
= (√3r²/4) × [12/(2πr² - 3√3r²)]
= 3√3r² / (2πr² - 3√3r²)
= 3√3 / (2π - 3√3)
Note: The original answer showed ratio of triangle to sector, not to segment. If the question asks for triangle to segment, the calculation above is correct. If it asks for triangle to sector (which seems more standard), then:
Ratio = (√3r²/4) / (πr²/6) = (√3/4) × (6/π) = (3√3)/(2π) = 3√3 : 2π (Showed)
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207829963_clwubt.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207829963_clwubt.jpeg"}]

[{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"Draw a tangent to a circle from a point outside.","marks":1,"answer":"[Construction of tangent from external point] – Assume drawn.
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207830251_z6ojnb.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207830251_z6ojnb.jpeg"},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Prove that, \(\angle ABC + \angle ADC = 180^\circ\).","marks":2,"answer":"Join A, O and C, O.
- \(\angle ABC = \frac{1}{2} \angle AOC\) (angle at center is double).
- \(\angle ADC = \frac{1}{2}\) reflex \(\angle AOC\).
- Adding: \(\angle ABC + \angle ADC = \frac{1}{2} (\angle AOC + \text{reflex} \angle AOC) = \frac{1}{2} \times 360° = 180°\). (Proved)
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207830252_s1b8kh.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207830252_s1b8kh.jpeg"},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Prove that, OE is the perpendicular bisector of the chord through the touch points AD.","marks":4,"answer":"Tangents AE and DE from E, touching at A and
- AE = DE (tangents from same point).
- In \(\triangle ODE\) and \(\triangle OAE\):
DE = AE, OD = OA (radii), OE common.
So, \(\triangle ODE \cong \triangle OAE\) (SSS).
Hence, \(\angle DOE = \angle AOE\).
- In \(\triangle ODP\) and \(\triangle OAP\):
OD = OA, OP common, included angles equal.
So, \(\triangle ODP \cong \triangle OAP\) (SAS).
Hence, DP = AP and ∠OPD = ∠OPA = 90°.
- Therefore, OE is perpendicular bisector of AD. (Proved)
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207830253_4vtuuc.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207830253_4vtuuc.jpeg"}]

[{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"Prove that, the diameter is the greatest chord of a circle.","marks":2,"answer":"Let BC be a chord, AB be diameter.
- In \(\triangle BOC\), OB + OC > BC.
- But OB + OC = OB + OA = AB.
- Therefore, AB > BC. (Proved)

- \(\angle PSR = \frac{1}{2}\) reflex \(\angle POR\).
- \(\angle PQR = \frac{1}{2} \angle POR\).
- Adding: \(\angle PSR + \angle PQR = \frac{1}{2} (\angle POR + \text{reflex} \angle POR) = \frac{1}{2} \times 360° = 180° = 2\) right angles. (Proved)
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207827903_ybicye.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207827903_ybicye.jpeg"},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Show that, \(\angle AMB + \angle CMD = 2\angle AEB\).","marks":4,"answer":"In \(\triangle AED\), exterior \(\angle AEB = \angle ADB + \angle CAD\).

[{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"The diameters of the two circles are 8cm. and 6 cm. respectively. If the circles touch each other externally, determine the distance between two centres of those circles.","marks":2,"answer":"Radii: \(r_1 = 4\) cm, \(r_2 = 3\) cm.
- Distance = \(r_1 + r_2 = 7\) cm. (Ans.)
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207830274_hvrd9i.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207830274_hvrd9i.jpeg"},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Prove that, \(\angle EDG + \angle EFG =\) Two right angles.","marks":4,"answer":"Join O, E and O, G.
- Reflex \(\angle EOG = 2\angle EFG\).
- \(\angle EOG = 2\angle EDG\).
- Adding: \(\angle EOG + \text{reflex} \angle EOG = 2(\angle EFG + \angle EDG)\).
- But sum = 360° = 4 right angles.
- So, \(\angle EFG + \angle EDG = 2\) right angles. (Proved)

- \(\angle DOE = 2\angle DGE\).
- \(\angle FOG = 2\angle FDG\).
- Adding: \(\angle DOE + \angle FOG = 2(\angle DGE + \angle FDG) = 2\angle DTE\). (Proved)
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207830274_04a1i.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207830274_04a1i.jpeg"}]

parts:
[{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"If circumference of a circle is 25 cm, then find the radius of the circle.","marks":2,"answer":"\(2\pi r = 25 \Rightarrow r = \frac{25}{2 \times 3.1416} \approx 3.98\) cm. (Ans.)
","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Prove that, AC = BC.","marks":4,"answer":"Given equal chords MN, OP. CA ⊥ MN, CB ⊥ OP.
- Perpendicular from centre bisects chord: MA = \(\frac{1}{2} MN\), OB = \(\frac{1}{2} OP\).
- Since MN = OP, MA = OB.
- In right triangles \(\triangle CMA\) and \(\triangle COB\):
Hypotenuse CM = CO (radii), MA = OB.
So, \(\triangle CMA \cong \triangle COB\).
Hence, AC = BC. (Proved)
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207830052_crq3r3.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207830052_crq3r3.jpeg"},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"If MN > OP, then prove that, AC < BC.","marks":4,"answer":"Let MN > OP. Then \(\frac{1}{2} MN > \frac{1}{2} OP\).
- In right triangles:
\(CN^2 = CA^2 + (\frac{1}{2} MN)^2\),
\(CP^2 = CB^2 + (\frac{1}{2} OP)^2\).
- Since CN = CP (radii),
\(CA^2 + (\frac{1}{2} MN)^2 = CB^2 + (\frac{1}{2} OP)^2\).
- Since \((\frac{1}{2} MN)^2 > (\frac{1}{2} OP)^2\), it follows that \(CA^2 < CB^2\).
- Therefore, AC < BC. (Proved)
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207830053_4e0p5q.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207830053_4e0p5q.jpeg"}]

[{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"PQRS is a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle and ∠PQR = 2∠PSR, then find the value of ∠PQR.","marks":2,"answer":"In cyclic quadrilateral PQRS:
- ∠PQR + ∠PSR = 180°.
- Given ∠PQR = 2∠PSR ⇒ 2∠PSR + ∠PSR = 180° ⇒ 3∠PSR = 180° ⇒ ∠PSR = 60°.
- So, ∠PQR = 120°. (Ans.)
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207830308_jmkg09.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207830308_jmkg09.jpeg"},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Prove that, ∠DCE = \(\frac{1}{2} \angle DME\).","marks":4,"answer":"Join DM, CM, EM.
- Exterior ∠DMO = ∠DCM + ∠CDM.
- In \(\triangle CMD\), ∠DCM = ∠CDM (since CM = DM).
- So, ∠DMO = 2∠DCM. Similarly, ∠EMO = 2∠ECM.
- Adding: ∠DME = 2(∠DCM + ∠ECM) = 2∠DCE.
- Hence, ∠DCE = \(\frac{1}{2} \angle DME\). (Proved)
","image":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207830309_f6k5i.jpeg","image_url":"https://idgogbisqacywbfnhdzy.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/question-images/1768207830309_f6k5i.jpeg"},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Prove that, the chords CD and CE are equidistant from the centre.","marks":4,"answer":"Draw MP ⊥ CD, MQ ⊥ CE.
- MP bisects CD, MQ bisects CE.
- Since CD = CE, halves are equal: CP = CQ.
- In right triangles \(\triangle CPM\) and \(\triangle CQM\):
Hypotenuse CM common, CP = CQ.
So, \(\triangle CPM \cong \triangle CQM\) (hypotenuse-side).
Hence, MP = MQ. (Proved)
